cards.title: Paradise's Four Rivers of Uncorrupted Water, Milk, Wine, and Purified Honey
cards.note: Surah 47:15 depicts the Garden with four rivers—water without pollution, milk of unchanged taste, delicious wine, and purified honey—matching the four rivers of honey, milk, wine, and oil around the City of Christ in the Apocalypse of Paul 22.

discussion.view: Commentators regard the four rivers of Surah 47:15 as a direct divine description of the unseen realities of Paradise awaiting believers.
discussion.reply: Genesis 2:10 names four earthly rivers flowing from Eden (Pishon, Gihon, Tigris, and Euphrates), whereas the late fourth-century Christian apocryphon Apocalypse of Paul (Chapter 22) transforms those four rivers into rivers of honey, milk, wine, and oil; Surah 47:15 incorporates this late antique four-beverage schema.

cards.quranEn: A parable of the Garden which is promised to the ones who guard (themselves): In it (there are) rivers of water without pollution, and rivers of milk – its taste does not change – and rivers of wine – delicious to the drinkers – and rivers of purified honey. In it (there is) every (kind of) fruit for them, and forgiveness from their Lord. (Are they) like those who remain in the Fire? They are given boiling water to drink, and it cuts their insides (to pieces).
quranHighlights: rivers of water without pollution, and rivers of milk – its taste does not change – and rivers of wine – delicious to the drinkers – and rivers of purified honey.

sources.title: Apocalypse of Paul (Visio Pauli — The Four Rivers of Milk, Honey, Wine, and Oil)
sources.ref: Apocalypse of Paul, Chapter 22 (tr. Alexander Walker, ANF Vol. 8)
sources.workSub: Apocalypse of Paul (Visio Pauli — The Four Rivers of Milk, Honey, Wine, and Oil)
sources.date: late 4th century AD (Greek / Syriac / Latin recensions)
sources.en: There was, moreover, a river of honey and a river of milk, and a river of wine and a river of oil. And I said to the angel : What are these rivers surrounding that city? And he says to me: These are the four rivers which flow sufficiently for those who are in this land of promise, of which the names are: the river of honey is called Fison, and the river of milk Euphrates, and the river of oil Gion, and the river of wine Tigris, such therefore they are for those who when placed in the world did not use the power of these things, but they hungered for these things and afflicted themselves for the sake of the Lord God: so that when these enter into this city, the Lord will assign them these things on high above all measure.
highlights: a river of honey and a river of milk, and a river of wine and a river of oil.
the river of honey is called Fison, and the river of milk Euphrates, and the river of oil Gion, and the river of wine Tigris

cards.title: 'In a Day, the Measure of Which Is a Thousand Years of What You Count'
cards.note: Surah 32:5 declares that the cosmic affair ascends to God 'in a day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count,' matching Psalm 90:4 (LXX 89:4), 2 Peter 3:8 ('with the Lord one day is like a thousand years'), and Jubilees 4:30.

discussion.view: Commentators interpret the thousand-year day of Surah 32:5 either as the span of cosmic administration or as the length of a day in the Hereafter.
discussion.reply: The formula equating one divine day with a thousand human years is an established Second Temple and New Testament exegetical tradition rooted in Psalm 90:4 (LXX 89:4) and formulated explicitly in Jubilees 4:30 ('one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens') and 2 Peter 3:8.

cards.quranEn: He directs the (whole) affair from the sky to the earth; then it will go up to Him in a day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count.
quranHighlights: in a day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count.

sources.title: Psalms (Septuagint LXX)

sources.title: Second Epistle of Peter (NASB)
sources.en: But do not let this one [fact] escape your notice, beloved, that with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.

sources.title: Book of Jubilees
sources.en: And he lacked seventy years of one thousand years; for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens and therefore was it written concerning the tree of knowledge: "On the day that ye eat thereof ye will die."
highlights: for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens
